item.title: Chaining Deep Link Injection with SQLi to Leak Sensitive Data from an iOS App
item.description:
This is my writeup for the Flipcoin Wallet iOS challenge by Mobile Hacking Labs - a two-part challenge involving deep link abuse and SQL injection that chains together really nicely.

Understanding the Challenge

The app is a crypto banking app with Flipcoin as its currency. Features:

  • Receive coins via QR code
  • Send coins to other accounts
  • Transaction history
  • Crypto news tab

The challenge description mentions SQLi and deeplink exploitation. The goal is to extract recovery keys of other users.

item.title: Exploiting SQLite Injection via Username Field Concatenation on Android
item.description:
This is my writeup for the FoodStore Android challenge by Mobile Hacking Labs - a straightforward but satisfying SQL injection challenge hidden inside a food delivery app.

Objective: Exploit a SQL Injection vulnerability in the signup function to register a Pro user (10,000 credits) and bypass normal restrictions.

Environment

  • Android app: com.mobilehackinglab.foodstore
  • Vulnerable class: DBHelper (uses SQLiteOpenHelper and execSQL with string concatenation)
  • DB: userdatabase.db, table users(id, username, password, address, isPro)
